newsitem.title: USA: Latest slate of Clinton nominees gets mixed reviews.
newsitem.headline: Latest slate of Clinton nominees gets mixed reviews.

text.p: Republican senators gave mixed reviews Friday to President Clinton's latest slate of Cabinet nominees, who must win Senate approval.
Republican-controlled committees will review the nominations before they are forwarded to the full Senate.

Senate Budget Committee Chairman Pete Domenici said the nomination of Federico Pena, the current transportation secretary, to be energy secretary may run into some trouble during the confirmation process in the Senate.

"I believe Secretary Pena may have some trouble being confirmed because he has little or no apparent experience in the major Energy Department missions," Domenici, a New Mexico Republican, said in a statement.
Pena's nomination will first go through the Senate Energy Committee, of which Domenici is a member.
"I look forward to lengthy discussions with him (Pena) about the department, and hope he gives me reasons to support his nomination," Domenici said.
Senate Banking Committee Chairman Alfonse D'Amato, a New York Republican, said he would support Andrew Cuomo's nomination for housing secretary.

Cuomo is currently an assistant secretary at the Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD). He is the son of former New York Gov. Mario Cuomo. There has been some speculation in New York political circles that the younger Cuomo might run against D'Amato for the Senate in 1998.
"I've worked with Andrew Cuomo and he'll make a fine secretary. I intend to support his nomination," D'Amato said in a statement. Cuomo's nomination must go before the Senate Banking Committee.

But another Republican on the Banking Committee was not as quick to endorse Cuomo. Sen. Lauch Faircloth, a Republican from North Carolina, said: "The last thing HUD needs is a big city liberal at its helm. I will closely scrutinize his nomination."

Senate Republican Leader Trent Lott of Mississippi only issued comments on two of the nominees -- Alexis Herman, a White House aide, for labor secretary and Rodney Slater, federal highway administrator, for transportation secretary.

Lott said he welcomed the opportunity to work with Herman toward the goal of economic growth and jobs creation. On Slater, Lott said he has "substantial experience" for the transportation post and he hoped Slater would address federal policy on automobile airbags during the confirmation process.

Sen. Christopher Bond, the Republican chairman of the Small Business Committee from Missouri, said the experience of Clinton's nominee to head up the Small Business Administration, Aida Alvarez, was not as well known as some of the previous agency heads.

"Ms. Alvarez' small business experience is not as well known. We will use the confirmation process to look into Ms. Alvarez' background to learn what experience and strengths she brings to this job," he said.
